method: Official public documentation and product pages, retrieved using web search and open. No account login or product trial.

sources.title: Send to Autopilot
supported_facts: Users may manually send plain text or CSV files to Autopilot.
Detected feedback is captured and deduplicated.
Plain-text submission can include a source link.
CSV line items are processed individually; the documentation requests a user email column for attribution.
sources.limitations: Feature availability and exact workflow have not been tested. No accuracy, speed or Chinese-language quality claim is made.

sources.title: AI Customer Feedback Management / Autopilot
supported_facts: The product page says users can open the original conversation.
The FAQ says an audit log shows captured, merged and organized items, and actions can be undone.
sources.limitations: Vendor capability claims, not an independently verified test. Customer case-study accuracy numbers were deliberately excluded.

sources.title: Dovetail AI
supported_facts: Dovetail indicates AI contributions and adds user avatars when summaries are edited or highlights accepted.
Chat answers are described as traceable to source material.
AI summaries and thematic clustering of highlights are documented; some capabilities have plan restrictions.
sources.limitations: No claim of universal plan availability, achieved accuracy or actual ease of use. Documentation has not been validated through a product trial.

sources.title: Review an item's insights
supported_facts: Linked feedback insights can be reviewed in a product item's Insights sidebar.
Users can unlink an insight or link it to a different item.
The More actions menu can jump directly to the source feedback item.
sources.limitations: The source URL redirected to a newer article. Claims use the opened current content, not the older search snippet. No hands-on test was performed.

analysis_inferences: Canny is a direct functional substitute for pasted-feedback extraction in this scenario.
Source traceability is not an exclusive differentiation for the proposed Echo product.
A compact human-review flow is a positioning hypothesis that requires testing against users' existing workflows.
The proposed prototype cannot yet establish production model accuracy or a commercial market advantage.
